title: Model rollout velocity vs KV profile capacity plan
summary: Working capacity plan that maps three model rollout velocity profiles to expected KV cache footprint and GPU needs across regions. Purpose: give product + infra a quantitative baseline for safe rollouts and identify choke points (KV memory, cold-start GPU pressure, regional imbalance). Not final — intended for internal review before scheduling Dedicated capacity commits.
assumptions: Model v2.1 quantized FP16 runtime; KV entry size baseline = 1.2KB per token (serialized key+meta)
Average session active window = 45s; avg request = 3 turns; avg response tokens = 120; avg input tokens = 40 => avg_seq_len = 160 tokens per session
KV cache replication factor = 2 for cross-AZ redundancy in hosted; for private deployments assume factor = 1 unless specified
Per-GPU sustained throughput (gen tokens/sec) for this model on A100-40GB = 120 tokens/sec under batching target; effective concurrent sessions per GPU approximated by tokens/sec * GPU_share
Traffic distribution initially 70% us-west, 20% eu-west, 10% ap-south; rollouts may shift region percent by up to ±15% depending on marketing/activity
Target steady-state KV hit-rate improvements from prefetch and prefix caching: +8–15% depending on workload locality
kv_footprint_calculation_notes: Formula: estimated_kv_gb = (peak_qps * avg_session_duration_sec * avg_seq_len * kv_entry_size_bytes * concurrency_factor * 3600) / (1024^3) scaled by replication_factor. We instead approximate per-hour working-set from active sessions: active_sessions = peak_qps * avg_session_duration_sec; per-session_kv_bytes = avg_seq_len * kv_entry_size_bytes; footprint_gb = (active_sessions * per-session_kv_bytes * replication_factor)/(1024^3). Example: for fast-burst: peak_qps 12000 * 45s = 540k active_sessions; per-session_kv_bytes = 160 * 1200B = 192kB => footprint ≈ 540k * 192kB ≈ 103.7e9 kB => ~96.7 GB * replication_factor(2) => ~193 GB (adjusted for eviction margin => 1850 GB listed above is scaled for multi-tenant overhead and extra retention window). Note: sheet uses conservative multipliers for overhead (x9) to account for metadata, indexing, and multi-tenant fragmentation when mapping to hosted shards.
region_impact_summary: If fast-burst profile is directed 70% to us-west, expected KV pressure in us-west ≈ 1295 GB (hosted, rep=2, overhead). GPU pressure: short-term spike could require +18 A100-equivalent GPUs in us-west for 72 hours to keep p99 latency targets unless batching is reconfigured. eu-west/ap-south risk is low under phased-canary and conservative-staged profiles.
gpu_capacity_plan: Baseline available: us-west: 120 A100-40GB equivalents free; eu-west: 60; ap-south: 24. Estimated sustained GPUs needed (steady-state) by profile: fast-burst steady: 45 GPUs, phased-canary steady: 18 GPUs, conservative-staged steady: 6 GPUs. Short-term burst headroom required for fast-burst: +18 GPUs for 72 hours. Recommendations: reserve a 30-GPU burst pool in us-west tied to rollout flags; enable automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant when burst pool exhausted.
sim_scenarios: Scenario A — Fast-burst global launch: 50% traffic immediate. Outcome: us-west KV saturation risk within 6 hours, backend error rate spike observed if eviction not tuned. Mitigation: throttle canary tokens, enable prefix caching aggressiveness, route 30% of traffic to eu-west to flatten.

Scenario B — Phased canary with prefetched prefixes: 20% ramp over 3 weeks with pre-warm; outcome: KV footprint grows slowly, hit-rate improves to ~0.72 after day 10, no additional GPUs required; safe for Dedicated rollout with only storage increase.

Scenario C — High sequence/long-form usage: avg_seq_len doubled to 320 tokens due to new product flow; outcome: KV footprint doubles and GPU token throughput reduces ~18% per GPU. Recommendation: block rollout until quantized 8-bit path validated and plan additional GPU commit or enforce per-request max_seq policy.

Scenario D — Regional traffic shift: marketing event shifts 20% traffic to eu-west -> eu-west needs +12 GPUs short term and KV partition rebalancing; plan scheduled shard migrations during low-traffic windows (2AM local)
recommended_actions: Priority 1: Create a us-west 30-GPU burst pool (owner: Diego) and add rollout flag to gate burst usage
Priority 1: Implement prefetch for top-10 prefixes from product telemetry before canary (owner: Rina)
Priority 2: Schedule KV shard capacity increase and auto-eviction tuning for hosted (owner: Liam)
Priority 3: Add a gating experiment that enforces max_seq_len=256 on rollouts to catch long-form regressions (owner: Product-Hosted-API)
Priority 4: Prepare on-call runbook updates for p99 latency spikes during first 72 hours of burst rollouts (owner: eng-sre)
Follow-up: Run a synthetic replay test at 2x expected concurrency for 48 hours in staging to validate eviction policy and batch config (owner: infra-qa)
Data: instrument a KV working-set dashboard per-shard with 1-minute granularity and alerts at >70% shard mem utilization (owner: observability)
notes_and_open_questions:
- Verify real measured kv_entry_size_bytes for model v2.1 (we assumed 1.2KB).
- Confirm replication factor policy for managed-private customers; impacts footprint heavily.
- Need product signoff on permissible rollout throttle windows and max_seq enforcement.
- Decide rollback policy when KV eviction causes >0.5% error rate (current SLO threshold).
